text:
Noah Cates scored his second goal of the season against Utah on Nov. 1, a top-shelf finish that put the Flyers ahead 3-1. Goals are a bonus for him. Evolving-Hockey had him 47th among 401 forwards last season at 2.1 wins above replacement, with the biggest share coming from the penalty kill and a defensive impact in the 97th percentile.

This season's version looks similar. He has 5 points in 18 games, his finishing is exactly on schedule (2 goals on 2.06 expected), and the Flyers are almost ten points better in their share of expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice than without. On a team that takes 41% of the expected goals at five on five, he's one of the few holding his ground.

His offense won't win headlines: Evolving-Hockey had his team creating fewer chances with him on (bottom 10%), and his skating sits in the 16th percentile for top speed. He's a 2017 fifth-round pick from Stillwater, Minnesota, who played for the U.S. at the 2022 Olympics. We project about 13 goals. In a Flyers season heading the wrong way, a reliable penalty killer is worth more than his points.
headline: Cates, the penalty killer
